text:
Let $x\ast y=x^{2}+y^{3}$ and $(x\ast 1)\ast 1=x\ast (1\ast 1)$.

Then a value of $2\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{4}+x^{2}-2}{x^{4}+x^{2}+2}\right )$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The star "*" in this context represents a binary operation, similar to addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (×), and division (÷). It is a custom operation defined by the problem statement, and the specific rules of the operation are provided in the problem. 

In this case, the operation "*" is defined by the equation $x\ast y=x^{2}+y^{3}$, which means if you have two numbers $x$ and $y$, then the result of applying the "*" operation to them is $x^{2}+y^{3}$. 

The problem also specifies an additional rule for this operation: $(x\ast 1)\ast 1=x\ast (1\ast 1)$, which needs to be taken into account when solving the problem. This is a type of "associativity" condition.
Given,

$x\ast y=x^{2}+y^{3}$

$\therefore$ $x\ast 1=x^{2}+1^{3}=x^{2}+1$

Now, $(x\quad \ast 1)\ast 1=(x^{2}+1)\ast 1$

$\Rightarrow (x\ast 1)\ast 1=(x^{2}+1)^{2}+1^{3}$

$\Rightarrow (x\ast 1)\ast 1=x^{4}+1+2x^{2}+1$

Also, $x\ast (1\ast 1)$

$=x\ast (1^{2}+1^{3})$

$=x\ast 2$

$=x^{2}+2^{3}$

$=x^{2}+8$

Given that,

$(x\quad \ast 1)\ast 1=x\ast (1\ast 1)$

$\therefore$ $x^{4}+1+2x^{2}+1=x^{2}+8$

$\Rightarrow x^{4}+x^{2}-6=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{4}+3x^{2}-2x^{2}-6=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}(x^{2}+3)-2(x^{2}+3)=0$

$\Rightarrow (x^{2}+3)(x^{2}-2)=0$

$\Rightarrow x^{2}=2,-3$

[$x^{2}=-3$ not possible as square of anything should be always positive]

$\therefore$ $x^{2}=2$

$\therefore$ Now,

$2\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{x^{4}+x^{2}-2}{x^{4}+x^{2}+2}\right )$

$=2\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{2^{2}+2-2}{2^{2}+2+2}\right )$

$=2\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{4}{8}\right )$

$=2\sin ^{-1}\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )$

$=2\times \frac{π}{6}$

$=\frac{π}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(e^{2x}-4)(6e^{2x}-5e^{x}+1)=0$

Let $e^{x}=t$

$\therefore$ $(t^{2}-4)(6t^{2}-5t+1)=0$

$\Rightarrow (t^{2}-4)(2t-1)(3t-1)=0$

$\therefore$ t = 2, $-$2, $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{3}$

$\therefore$ $e^{x}=2\Rightarrow x=\ln 2$

$e^{x}=-2$ (not possible)

$e^{x}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=-\ln 2$

$e^{x}=\frac{1}{3}\Rightarrow x=-\ln 3$

$\therefore$ Sum of all real roots

$=\ln 2-\ln 2-\ln 3$

$=-\ln 3$

text:
Let the system of linear equations

x + y + $α$z = 2

3x + y + z = 4

x + 2z = 1

have a unique solution (x${}^{\ast }$, y${}^{\ast }$, z${}^{\ast }$). If ($α$, x${}^{\ast }$), (y${}^{\ast }$, $α$) and (x${}^{\ast }$, $-$y${}^{\ast }$) are collinear points, then the sum of absolute values of all possible values of $α$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The coefficient determinant is

$\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & α \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{array}\right |=1(2-0)-1(6-1)+α(0-1)=-3-α,$

so a unique solution requires $α\neq -3$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives $2x+(1-α)z=2$, and the third gives $x=1-2z$. Then $2-4z+(1-α)z=2$, i.e. $-(3+α)z=0$, so $z^{\ast }=0$, $x^{\ast }=1$, and the second equation gives $y^{\ast }=4-3=1$.

The points $(α,1)$, $(1,α)$ and $(1,-1)$ are collinear, so

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} α & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & α & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=α(α+1)-1(1-1)+1(-1-α)=α^{2}-1=0.$

Thus $α=\pm 1$, both different from $-3$, and the sum of the absolute values is $1+1=2$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} \frac{\sin (x-[x])}{x[x]} & , & x\in (-2,-1) \\ \max \{2x,3[|x|]\} & , & |x|<1 \\ 1 & , & otherwise \end{array} \right.$

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{lll} \frac{\sin (x+2)}{x+2} & , & x\in (-2,-1) \\ 0 & , & x\in (-1,0] \\ 2x & , & x\in (0,1) \\ 1 & , & otherwise \end{array} \right.$

text: Let the maximum area of the triangle that can be inscribed in the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{4}=1,a>2$, having one of its vertices at one end of the major axis of the ellipse and one of its sides parallel to the y-axis, be $6\sqrt{3}$. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here $b^{2}=4$. Take the vertex at the end $A(a,0)$ of the major axis; the side parallel to the $y$-axis is the chord $BB^{'}$ with $B(a\cos θ,2\sin θ)$ and $B^{'}(a\cos θ,-2\sin θ)$, $0<θ<π$.


[IMG]

$BB^{'}=4\sin θ$ and the distance of $A$ from $BB^{'}$ is $a-a\cos θ$, so the area is

$\Delta (θ)=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot 4\sin θ\cdot a(1-\cos θ)=2a\sin θ-a\sin 2θ$

$\Delta ^{'}(θ)=2a(\cos θ-\cos 2θ)=-2a(2\cos θ+1)(\cos θ-1)$

$\Delta ^{'}(θ)=0$ gives $\cos θ=-\dfrac{1}{2}$ ($\cos θ=1$ gives no triangle). $\Delta ^{'}$ changes from positive to negative there, so the area is maximum at $θ=\dfrac{2π}{3}$:

$\Delta _{\max }=2a\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \dfrac{3}{2}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}a}{2}=6\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow a=4$

$e=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{4}{16}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$\because$ A(1, $α$), B($α$, 0) and C(0, $α$) are the vertices of $\Delta$ABC and area of $\Delta$ABC = 4

$\therefore$ $\left |\frac{1}{2}\right |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & α & 1 \\ α & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & α & 1 \end{array}\left |\right |=4$

$\Rightarrow \left |1(0-α)-α(α)+α^{2}\right |=8$

$\Rightarrow α=\pm 8$

Now, $(α,-α),(-α,α)$ and $(α^{2},β)$ are collinear

$\Rightarrow 8(8-β)+8(-8-64)+1(-8β-8\times 64)=0$

$\Rightarrow 8-β-72-β-64=0$

$\Rightarrow β=-64$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The probabilities add to 1: $k+2k+4k+6k+8k=21k=1$, so $k=\dfrac{1}{21}$.

The event $1<X<4$ is $X\in \{2,3\}$; together with $X\leq 2$ only $X=2$ remains, so $P(1<X<4\text{and}X\leq 2)=P(X=2)=4k$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Let $\widehat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$ be two unit vectors such that $|(\widehat{a}+\hat{b})+2(\widehat{a}\times \hat{b})|=2$. If $θ$ $\in$ (0, $π$) is the angle between $\widehat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$, then among the statements :

(S1) : $2|\widehat{a}\times \hat{b}|=|\widehat{a}-\hat{b}|$

(S2) : The projection of $\widehat{a}$ on ($\widehat{a}$ + $\hat{b}$) is $\frac{1}{2}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\hat{a}\times \hat{b}$ is perpendicular to both $\hat{a}$ and $\hat{b}$, $(\hat{a}+\hat{b})\cdot (\hat{a}\times \hat{b})=0$. Squaring the given condition:

$|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|^{2}+4|\hat{a}\times \hat{b}|^{2}=4\Rightarrow (2+2\cos θ)+4\sin ^{2}θ=4$

$\Rightarrow 2\cos θ+4-4\cos ^{2}θ=2\Rightarrow 2\cos ^{2}θ-\cos θ-1=0\Rightarrow (2\cos θ+1)(\cos θ-1)=0$

As $θ\in (0,π)$, $\cos θ\neq 1$, so $\cos θ=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, that is, $θ=\dfrac{2π}{3}$.

(S1): $2|\hat{a}\times \hat{b}|=2\sin \dfrac{2π}{3}=\sqrt{3}$ and $|\hat{a}-\hat{b}|=\sqrt{2-2\cos θ}=\sqrt{2+1}=\sqrt{3}$, so (S1) is true.

(S2): $|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|=\sqrt{2+2\cos θ}=1$ and $\hat{a}\cdot (\hat{a}+\hat{b})=1+\cos θ=\dfrac{1}{2}$, so the projection of $\hat{a}$ on $\hat{a}+\hat{b}$ is $\dfrac{\hat{a}\cdot (\hat{a}+\hat{b})}{|\hat{a}+\hat{b}|}=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and (S2) is true.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: The number of 7-digit numbers which are multiples of 11 and are formed using all the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The digit sum is $1+2+3+4+5+7+9=31$. Let $S_{1}$ be the sum of the digits in the four odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th) and $S_{2}$ the sum in the three even places, so $S_{1}+S_{2}=31$.

The number is divisible by 11 exactly when $S_{1}-S_{2}=2S_{1}-31$ is a multiple of 11. Since $1+2+3+4\leq S_{1}\leq 4+5+7+9$, i.e. $10\leq S_{1}\leq 25$, this gives $S_{1}-S_{2}=\pm 11$.

Case $S_{1}=21,S_{2}=10$: the three even-place digits are $\{1,2,7\}$, $\{1,4,5\}$ or $\{2,3,5\}$, leaving $\{3,4,5,9\}$, $\{2,3,7,9\}$ or $\{1,4,7,9\}$ for the odd places. Count $=3\times 3!\times 4!=432$.

Case $S_{1}=10,S_{2}=21$: the only three digits with sum 21 are $\{5,7,9\}$, leaving $\{1,2,3,4\}$ for the odd places. Count $=3!\times 4!=144$.

Total $=432+144=576$.

Hence, the answer is 576.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift

text: Let a circle C : (x $-$ $h)^{2} + (y$ $-$ $k)^{2} = r^{2}, k > 0$, touch the x-axis at (1, 0). If the line x + y = 0 intersects the circle C at P and Q such that the length of the chord PQ is 2, then the value of h + k + r is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Here, $OM^{2}=OP^{2}-PM^{2}$

$\left (\frac{|1+r|}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}=r^{2}-1$

$\therefore$ $r^{2}-2r-3=0$

$\therefore$ $r=3$

$\therefore$ Equation of circle is

$(x-1)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=3^{2}$

$\therefore$ h = 1, k = 3, r = 3

$\therefore$ $h+k+r=7$

text: Let the hyperbola $H:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-y^{2}=1$ and the ellipse $E:3x^{2}+4y^{2}=12$ be such that the length of latus rectum of H is equal to the length of latus rectum of E. If $e_{H}$ and $e_{E}$ are the eccentricities of H and E respectively, then the value of $12\left (e_{H}^{2}+e_{E}^{2}\right )$ is equal to $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $H:\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{1}=1$

$\therefore$ Length of latus rectum $=\frac{2}{a}$

$E:\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{3}=1$

Length of latus rectum $=\frac{6}{2}=3$

$\because$ $\frac{2}{a}=3\Rightarrow a=\frac{2}{3}$

$\therefore$ $12\left (e_{H}^{2}+e_{E}^{2}\right )=12\left (1+\frac{9}{4}\right )+\left (1-\frac{3}{4}\right )=42$

text: Let $P_{1}$ be a parabola with vertex (3, 2) and focus (4, 4) and $P_{2}$ be its mirror image with respect to the line x + 2y = 6. Then the directrix of $P_{2}$ is $x + 2y = ____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 24th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Focus = (4, 4) and vertex = (3, 2)

$\therefore$ Point of intersection of directrix with axis of parabola = A = (2, 0)

Image of A(2, 0) with respect to line x + 2y = 6 is $B(x_{2}, y_{2})$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x_{2}-2}{1}=\frac{y_{2}-0}{2}=\frac{-2(2+0-6)}{5}$

$\therefore$ $B(x_{2},y_{2})=\left (\frac{18}{5},\frac{16}{5}\right )$.

Point B is point of intersection of directrix with axis of parabola $P_{2}$.

$\therefore$ $x+2y=λ$ must have point $\left (\frac{18}{5},\frac{16}{5}\right )$

$\therefore$ $x+2y=10$
